proposals.before: In the eighth year Cai Qian slipped into Dinghai to offer incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng surprised him, and Qian escaped only with his life. Changgeng pursued him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet was out of provisions and its sails in tatters. Qian then feigned surrender to Governor Yude, who sent Circuit Intendant Qing Lai of Xing-Quan-Yong to Sansha to negotiate. Yude abruptly ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to harbor, and Qian used the respite to refit his ships and escape.
proposals.after: In the eighth year Cai Qian slipped into Dinghai to offer incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng surprised him, and Qian escaped only with his life. Changgeng pursued him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet was out of provisions and its sails in tatters. Qian then feigned surrender to Governor-general Yude, who sent Circuit Intendant Qing Lai of Xing-Quan-Yong to Sansha to negotiate. Yude abruptly ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to harbor, and Qian used the respite to refit his ships and escape.
proposals.reason: Chinese 總督玉德 is governor-general, not the same office as 巡撫 (governor) used for Ruan Yuan in s0016; the idiomatic gloss should preserve the rank distinction.

proposals.before: In the summer of the ninth year, Lian Zong led more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng. An edict called for punishment of Fujian officers who had failed to reinforce, and Changgeng was placed in overall command of the naval forces of both provinces.
proposals.after: In the summer of the ninth year, Qian led more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng. An edict called for punishment of Fujian officers who had failed to reinforce, and Changgeng was placed in overall command of the naval forces of both provinces.
proposals.reason: Adjacent units concern Cai Qian (牽); 連宗八十餘 is almost certainly a corruption of 牽率八十餘, so English should not invent a separate leader Lian Zong.

proposals.before: In the summer of the ninth year Lian Zong led more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng; an edict ordered punishment for Fujian officers who failed to reinforce; Changgeng took overall command of the naval forces of the two provinces.
proposals.after: In the summer of the ninth year Qian led more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng; an edict ordered punishment for Fujian officers who failed to reinforce; Changgeng took overall command of the naval forces of the two provinces.
proposals.reason: Same restoration: treat corrupted 連宗 as 牽率 and keep Qian as the subject in the literal English.

proposals.before: In the eleventh year he died, and his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng he died, and his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.
proposals.reason: Literal English omits the Xianfeng reign that 十一年 continues from preceding units; the idiomatic rendering correctly retains it.

proposals.before: He received generous posthumous care, was given the posthumous name Wuzhuang, and was granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Captain combined.
proposals.after: He received generous posthumous care, was given the posthumous name Wuzhuang, and his heirs were granted the combined hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Captain.
proposals.reason: 予…世職 confers hereditary ranks on the heirs rather than as offices of the deceased; the idiomatic English already reflects this.

proposals.before: Delu served ten years as Fujian naval commander-in-chief, repeatedly memorializing on coastal defense and revising naval ship regulations, all of which were adopted.
proposals.after: Delu served ten years as Fujian naval commander-in-chief, repeatedly memorializing on pursuit and capture matters and revising naval ship regulations, all of which were adopted.
proposals.reason: Chinese 緝捕事宜 means pursuit and capture of pirates/criminals, not coastal defense.

proposals.before: The next day they tried again to intercept and encircle him. Qian fought as he fled, and by noon the pursuit had crossed the Black Water Sea into the deep ocean.
proposals.after: The next day they tried again to intercept and encircle him. Qian fought as he fled, and by noon the pursuit had crossed the Black Water Sea and seen green water.
proposals.reason: Chinese 見綠水 means they saw green water; the idiomatic invents 'deep ocean'.

proposals.before: Following Lianggong in pursuit of Cai Qian, Buyun with forty men drove his boat straight against Qian's flagship in fierce combat; his vessel was small and no match; seeing the two commanders-in-chief arrive, he quickly threw fire pots to burn the bandit ship, hooked the rail with a long halberd, led several soldiers in leaping aboard, fought hand to hand at close quarters, and destroyed Qian's wife and her followers.
proposals.after: Following Lianggong in pursuit of Cai Qian, Buyun with forty men drove his boat straight against Qian's flagship in fierce combat; his vessel was small and no match; seeing the two commanders-in-chief arrive, he quickly threw fire pots to burn the bandit ship, hooked the rail with a long halberd, led several soldiers in leaping aboard, fought hand to hand at close quarters, and killed Qian's wife and her followers.
proposals.reason: 殲 of persons should be killed, not destroyed.

proposals.before: An edict praised Songnian's valor in destroying the ringleader, granted him the peacock feather, and gave him the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
proposals.after: An edict praised Songnian's valor in destroying the ringleader, granted him the peacock feather, and granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
proposals.reason: 世職 is a hereditary privilege for descendants, not an office given solely to Songnian personally; the idiomatic rendering already reflects this.

proposals.before: A military licentiate, he served in the navy under Li Changgeng, accumulated merit in repeated campaigns, and rose to brigade colonel on the provincial commander's staff.
proposals.after: A military licentiate, he served in the navy under Li Changgeng, accumulated merit, and rose to brigade colonel on the provincial commander's staff.
proposals.reason: Chinese 積功 does not specify 'repeated campaigns'; that phrase is an unsupported addition.

proposals.before: defeated Zhu Fen and Wushi Er at Gongzai Sea, and under Li Changgeng pursued and routed them at Jiazi Sea on the Fujian-Guangdong border.
proposals.after: again attacked Zhu Fen and Wushi Er at Gongzai Sea, and under Li Changgeng pursued and routed them at Jiazi Sea on the Fujian-Guangdong border.
proposals.reason: Chinese 又擊 means again attacked; idiomatic 'defeated' omits 又 and overstates the verb relative to the parallel literal.

proposals.before: When Guoliang died he acted as regional commander of the Left Wing Town.
proposals.after: When Guoliang died he acted as regional commander of the Left Wing Garrison.
proposals.reason: 鎮 here is a Qing regional garrison command, not an ordinary town; 'Left Wing Town' mistranslates 左翼鎮.

proposals.before: In the fourteenth year he destroyed the bandit leader Zongbing Bao on the open sea and besieged the remainder of his force.
proposals.after: In the fourteenth year he destroyed the bandit leader Regional Commander Bao on the open sea and besieged the remainder of his force.
proposals.reason: 匪首總兵保 uses 總兵 as an office-title nickname before the personal name 保; transliterating the whole as 'Zongbing Bao' obscures that title-plus-name structure.

proposals.before: In the fourteenth year he attacked and destroyed the bandit chieftain Zongbing Bao on the outer sea and besieged the rest of his faction.
proposals.after: In the fourteenth year he attacked and destroyed the bandit chieftain Regional Commander Bao on the outer sea and besieged the rest of his faction.
proposals.reason: Same office-title-plus-name reading of 總兵保 as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: Posthumous care was granted and he was given the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
proposals.after: Posthumous care was granted and his family was given the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
proposals.reason: 予雲騎尉世職 awards a hereditary office to the deceased's line, not a personal appointment held by the dead man himself.

proposals.before: Gain and loss form a forest of examples—therefore there is no luck in it!
proposals.after: The record of gains and losses leaves no room for chance!
proposals.reason: 得失之林 is a classical 'lessons of success and failure' idiom; the calque 'forest of examples' is opaque in English.

decisions.after: In the eighth year Cai Qian slipped into Dinghai to offer incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng surprised him, and Qian escaped only with his life. Changgeng pursued him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet was out of provisions and its sails in tatters. Qian then feigned surrender to Governor-General Yude, who sent Circuit Intendant Qing Lai of Xing-Quan-Yong to Sansha to negotiate. Yude abruptly ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to harbor, and Qian used the respite to refit his ships and escape.
decisions.reason: The source calls Yude a 總督, distinct from a 巡撫. The proposal fixes the rank, but the established title styling in this chapter is Governor-General, with both elements capitalized before a name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 偽乞降於總督玉德

decisions.after: In the summer of the ninth year, Cai Qian and Zhu Fen entered Fujian with a combined fleet of more than eighty vessels and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng. An edict called for punishment of Fujian officers who had failed to reinforce, and Changgeng was placed in overall command of the naval forces of both provinces.
decisions.reason: Lian Zong is spurious: an external witness preserves the rare fleet character 䑸 where the local text has been flattened to 宗. The preceding sentence says Cai Qian joined Zhu Fen, so the subject is their combined fleet, not Qian alone.

sourceWitness.citation: Qing Shi Gao, vol. 350, https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/清史稿/卷350
sourceWitness.excerpt: 遂與之合。九年夏，連䑸八十餘入閩，戕總兵胡振聲

decisions.after: In the summer of the ninth year Cai Qian and Zhu Fen brought a combined fleet of more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng; an edict ordered punishment for Fujian officers who failed to reinforce; Changgeng took overall command of the naval forces of the two provinces.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly removes a nonexistent person but wrongly treats Qian as sole subject. The rare character 䑸 means a fleet, and the preceding context establishes the joined forces of Cai Qian and Zhu Fen.

decisions.reason: 緝捕事宜 concerns measures for pursuit and capture, not the broader subject of coastal defense. Naming pirates makes the contextual object clear and produces natural English without enlarging the claim.

decisions.after: The next day they tried again to intercept and encircle him. Qian fought as he fled, and by noon the pursuit had crossed the Black Water Sea and reached green water.
decisions.reason: 見綠水 reports reaching or sighting green water after crossing the Black Water Sea; deep ocean is an unsupported interpretation. Reached green water is faithful and less awkward than the proposal's seen green water.

decisions.reason: The object of 殲 is Cai Qian's wife and her followers, so killed is the idiomatic English verb. The proposal changes only that mistranslated verb and agrees with the existing event and death claims.

decisions.after: An edict praised Songnian's valor in destroying the ringleader, granted him the peacock feather, and granted his family the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
decisions.reason: 雲騎尉世職 is a hereditary rank transmitted through the family, not a personal office. The proposal fixes rank but still leaves the beneficiary ambiguous; the idiomatic field correctly makes the family explicit.

decisions.reason: 積功 states that Xu Songnian accumulated merit but does not itself specify repeated campaigns. Removing that unsupported embellishment leaves clear, grammatical English and preserves the career progression.

decisions.reason: 又擊 means attacked again, whereas the following 追敗之 expressly supplies the later defeat. The proposal preserves that distinction and the lower-case continuation required after the preceding semicolon.

decisions.reason: 左翼鎮 is a named Qing military garrison command, not an ordinary town. Garrison correctly conveys the institutional sense and agrees with the already accurate idiomatic rendering.

decisions.reason: 總兵保 is presented earlier as the established name of one of the five Guangdong pirate bands or leaders. Expanding it to Regional Commander Bao falsely turns the sobriquet into a current Qing office; Zongbing Bao should remain.

decisions.reason: The chapter uses 總兵保 as a pirate sobriquet in its list of five Guangdong bands or leaders. Regional Commander Bao misleadingly recasts that name as an official title, so the existing Zongbing Bao is preferable.
